# Project Instructions

- Preserve and improve the game's sound design and physical ball dynamics by default.
- When changing gameplay, avoid flattening or removing impactful sound effects unless explicitly requested.
- When changing ball behavior, prefer responsive, believable motion with bounce, spin, momentum, and clear audiovisual feedback over simplified placeholder motion.
- If a tradeoff is necessary, keep the game feeling dynamic and expressive rather than quiet or mechanically flat.
